events.content: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure OCI revenue Q2 FY2027 quarterly results

Oracle has not yet reported OCI (Cloud Infrastructure/IaaS) revenue for Q2 FY2027, the quarter ending November 30, 2026; its next earnings release is expected in mid-December 2026. [[1, 2]] 

Oracle’s Q2 FY2027 guidance is for **total cloud revenue**—OCI plus SaaS—to grow **65%–71% year over year in U.S. dollars**, rather than providing a standalone OCI-revenue dollar forecast. [[3]] 

For reference, OCI revenue in Q1 FY2027 was **$7.4 billion**, up **121% year over year**. [[3]]

tool_arguments.query: Oracle OCI remaining performance obligations RPO AI contracts Q1 FY2027

events.content: Oracle OCI remaining performance obligations RPO AI contracts Q1 FY2027

**Oracle’s FY2027 AI-cloud/RPO position:** At the end of fiscal Q1 2027 (August 31, 2026), Oracle reported **$664 billion of remaining performance obligations (RPO)**, up **$209 billion year over year**. [[1]] 

Oracle said it booked **more than $30 billion of additional AI-cloud contracts** during the quarter, as demand for AI training and inference services continued to exceed available supply. [[1]] 

OCI/IaaS revenue was **$7.4 billion in Q1 FY2027**, up **121% year over year**; combined cloud revenue (IaaS plus SaaS) was **$11.6 billion**, up **62%**. [[1]] 

For conversion timing, Oracle’s Q1 FY2027 filing indicates approximately **13%** of RPO—about **$86 billion**—is expected to be recognized in the next 12 months, while approximately **50%** is expected within 36 months. [[2]] 

The important analytical caveat is that RPO is contracted, unrecognized revenue rather than OCI revenue guidance, and Oracle does not disclose the portion of the $664 billion backlog attributable specifically to OCI or to individual AI customers. [[2]] 

For full FY2027, Oracle guided to at least **$90 billion of total revenue** and **$8.10 of non-GAAP EPS**; it did not provide a standalone full-year OCI revenue target in the cited earnings release. [[1]] 

Oracle also stated that the structure of the new AI contracts creates **no incremental impact on its capital-raising plans**, suggesting a material role for prepayment, customer-supplied hardware, or other capital-light contract structures rather than Oracle solely funding all incremental compute capacity. [[1]]

Sources:
[S2.1] Oracle Announces Q1 Results Driven by Triple Digit Growth in Cloud Infrastructure Revenues — https://www.oracle.com/news/announcement/q1fy27-earnings-release-2026-09-10/
[S2.2] Oracle Q1: Half of $664B RPO Expected as Revenue in 3 Years — https://financefeeds.com/oracle-q1-fy27-rpo-664-billion-36-month-conversion/

events.content:
**Net worth.** Forbes estimated Larry Ellison’s real-time net worth at **$167.2 billion as of October 17, 2026**, a figure that changes with market prices and reflects the change since the prior trading day’s close. [[1]] 
The wealth is overwhelmingly tied to Oracle: Bloomberg describes Ellison as Oracle’s founder and largest shareholder, owning **around 40%** of the company, while Oracle’s 2026 proxy states that he is its founder, executive chair, CTO, and largest shareholder. [[2, 3]]

**Major outside-Oracle investments and assets.** 

- **Skydance / Paramount:** The Ellison family is the controlling shareholder of Paramount Skydance through Harbor Lights Entertainment, with approximately **77.5% of Class A voting stock** and **47.3% of combined Class A plus non-voting Class B stock** reported in the company’s Q1 2026 Form 10-Q. [[4]]
- **Lānaʻi, Hawaii:** Through Pūlama Lānaʻi, Ellison owns **98% of the island’s acreage**, acquired in 2012 for about **$300 million**; the holdings include substantial land, housing, a water utility, and two Four Seasons resorts. [[5]]
- **Tesla:** Ellison’s most recently clearly disclosed stake was about **1.4% of Tesla**, according to Tesla’s 2022 proxy, but he left Tesla’s board in June 2022 and Bloomberg notes that the stake has not subsequently been publicly updated. [[2]]
- **Sports and leisure assets:** Bloomberg identifies investments in a sailing team and the Indian Wells tennis event, in addition to his Lānaʻi real estate. [[2]]
- **X/Twitter:** Ellison made a **$1 billion equity commitment** toward Elon Musk’s 2022 acquisition of Twitter, within a $7.14 billion group of outside equity commitments disclosed for the transaction. [[6]]

**Important caveat.** These disclosed holdings should not be interpreted as a complete, mark-to-market investment portfolio: Ellison’s externally visible wealth is concentrated in Oracle, while Lānaʻi, resorts, sports properties, private-company interests, and the family’s Paramount/Skydance control position are comparatively illiquid and not consistently publicly valued. [[1, 2, 4]]
